tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-13 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the first European consumer readings in six weeks on its side and the tape's disagreement narrower. German consumer confidence (GfK) reads -30.8 for November from -30.6 and the euro area's flash reads -17.9 for October from -16.5 (Newsquawk, undated): low and edging lower, so the condition 'to D on a European consumer reading that is not falling' is tested and not met. The United States reading is disputed (University of Michigan 51.0, a three-month high, 6 November, against outlets describing it as falling). Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: D now, D prior at the industry (C at last week's reading), with Online retail A, Hotels B (A last week), Apparel B and Physical retail B, so the second condition (the industry at C or better with Hotels and Online retail holding A) is not met either. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). Counter-case: the survey readings are undated headlines, four sectors still read A or B, 20 Pool stocks sit under this letter, and cyclicals led over the last week. To D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or the industry back at C with Online retail holding A.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged, with a stated disagreement. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): discretionary spend under a low United States consumer reading (University of Michigan 48.1) and high-multiple platform cases hit by the discount rate; but the European consumer was not read this week, and relative strength says A now, A prior (two readings two months apart) with the turning note's third hypothesis placing Allegro and ASOS in the de-rated-consumer rotation. Held at D because the two reasons that set it still stand and the evidence against it is a rank and a brainstorm; moves to C on a European consumer reading that is not falling.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Poland this week; Goldman's note (22 Oct) that emerging-market sovereign spreads are widening with US rate volatility is general, not Polish, and the condition for D (a source reading Polish spreads wider, or a third memo naming the sovereign) is not met; no memo carried a congruence line this week. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Twelve of the 149 Pool stocks are Polish, seven of them banks, so this is still the country row most likely to move. Relative strength is not graded by country.
